summary:
Agro Mars offers a space simulation experience through a cooperative RPG video game for up to four players, combining survival, construction, and strategic resource management.
Our proposal aims to turn NASA's scientific data, such as temperature, radiation, light cycles, and environmental conditions, into variables that directly influence the development of a space farm.
Players will need to design agricultural systems, select crops, manage nutrients, and optimize water and energy consumption. Every decision will have consequences for the colony's productivity and stability, while unexpected challenges will test their ability to adapt.
The project aims to demonstrate how science and technology can become interactive learning tools. The main challenge will be to develop a self-sustaining colony through food production, resource recycling, and the use of renewable energy, ultimately reducing its dependence on Earth to zero.
details:
Agro Mars is a proposed cooperative role-playing game (RPG) focused on survival and space simulation for up to four players. It combines adventure, open-ended building, resource management, and scientific learning. Designed for players ages 12 and up, the game aims to recreate the challenges of establishing a self-sufficient human colony on Mars.

The experience will begin in a preparation room where players will select the resources, equipment, and supplies they will use to start their mission. During the early stages, they will receive support from Earth, but this assistance will gradually decrease as they develop their own resource production and recovery systems.

Players will be able to freely build and expand their colony, organizing it into specialized areas for vertical farming, energy generation, water purification, recycling, research, and crew well-being.

The game aims to incorporate NASA scientific data on Martian temperatures, solar radiation, seasons, and atmospheric conditions. These variables will affect energy production, crop growth, and the unexpected challenges players will face.

Technological systems will be scalable. For example, a photovoltaic installation could start with a nominal design capacity of 50 W and increase its output by adding solar panels, batteries, and infrastructure upgrades. Each expansion will require resources and will be subject to physical and environmental limitations.

Vertical farming will allow players to grow crops such as lettuce, radishes, spinach, and microgreens, taking into account their growth cycles and requirements for water, nutrients, energy, and space. The game also plans to incorporate biodigesters, purification systems, and waste treatment technologies to recover water and nutrients, as well as chemical processes to make use of Martian resources.

Each astronaut will have physical and emotional needs, including hunger, thirst, sleep, hygiene, physiological needs, and mood. Players will need to manage their activities and develop recreational spaces to maintain the crew's well-being.

Agro Mars aims to introduce young people to space exploration through an interactive experience that progressively teaches concepts related to engineering, chemistry, biochemistry, sustainable agriculture, and resource management.

The game will include an AI-powered educational assistant designed to answer scientific questions and explain concepts in an easy-to-understand way, using verifiable information as a reference.

The project also proposes an innovation room where players can submit ideas for new equipment and technological solutions. These contributions could be organized as community proposals with educational and scientific value, without assuming they will be directly used by NASA.

Agro Mars is currently in the planning and conceptual design phase. The team has not yet selected a game engine, programming languages, or design and modeling tools.

The team plans to evaluate technologies that support environmental simulations, modular construction, resource management systems, cooperative gameplay, and an AI-powered educational assistant.

Its main innovation lies in integrating scientific knowledge into a building and survival system where players' decisions directly affect how the colony operates.

The freedom to design facilities, research technologies, expand systems, and respond to unexpected challenges will allow each team to develop different strategies.

Additionally, the combination of scalable technology, a circular economy, astronaut well-being, educational artificial intelligence, and community participation aims to turn the game into an environment for learning and experimentation.

The design takes into account Mars' actual environmental conditions, limited resource availability, system safety, sustainability, human needs, educational accessibility, and progressive difficulty for players ages 12 and up.

The proposal draws on the interdisciplinary collaboration of students from Chemical, Electromechanical, Industrial, and Biochemical Engineering.
